original_value: The sensor cloud is a combination of cloud computing with a wireless sensor network (WSN) which provides an easy to scale and efficient computing infrastructure for real-time application. A sensor cloud should be energy efficient as the life of the battery in the sensor is limited and there is a huge consumption of energy in the data centre in running the servers to provide storage. In this paper, we have classified energy-efficient techniques for sensor cloud into different categories and analyzed each technology by using various parameters. Usage percentage of each parameter for every technology is calculated and for all technologies on average is also calculated. From our analysis, we found that most of the energy-efficient techniques ignore quality of service (QoS) parameters, scalability, and network lifetime. Multiparameter optimization including other QoS parameters along with energy may be the future direction of research. Our study will be helpful for researchers to get information regarding current methods used for an energy-efficient sensor cloud and also to build advanced systems in the future.

result.paraphrase: A sensor cloud combines cloud computing with a wireless sensor network (WSN), creating a scalable and efficient infrastructure for real-time applications. Because sensor batteries have limited life and data centers consume substantial energy to run servers for storage, a sensor cloud should be energy efficient. In this paper, we categorize energy-efficient techniques for sensor clouds and evaluate each technology using various parameters. We also calculate the usage percentage of each parameter for every technology, as well as the overall average across all technologies. Our analysis shows that most energy-efficient techniques overlook quality of service (QoS) parameters, scalability, and network lifetime. Future research may focus on multiparameter optimization that includes QoS factors alongside energy. This study will help researchers understand current methods for building an energy-efficient sensor cloud and developing advanced systems in the future.
